findings.title: V2 client permissions throw UnsupportedOperationException on paths that used to work
findings.body: Before this change, `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` returned the V1 `ClientPermissions`. Now it returns `ClientPermissionsV2`, and that class throws `UnsupportedOperationException` from `canExchangeTo`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource` and `getPermissions`. Any caller that reaches these through `AdminPermissions.management(...).clients()` in a realm with ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled now gets an unhandled 500 instead of an allow or deny. Examples: the legacy token-exchange permission check (`canExchangeTo`) and the client `management/permissions` admin endpoint (`isPermissionsEnabled` / `getPermissions`). I could not see every caller. Return a safe value, such as `false`, an empty map or null, or deny with a ForbiddenException instead of throwing a runtime exception. Alternatively, make sure these endpoints are unreachable under V2.

findings.title: Test rotates the secret of the client the admin test client logs in with
findings.body: `testConfigureOnlyOneClient` calls `generateNewSecret()` and then `invalidateRotatedSecret()` on `myclient`. That is the confidential client (secret `mysecret`) that `realmAdminClient` and the other FGAP tests use to get tokens. The `@AfterEach` cleanup only removes permissions, so after this test the managed realm's `myclient` no longer accepts `mysecret`. Any later token fetch or refresh with the injected admin client fails with 401, depending on test order. The same test class also leaves other changes behind: the renamed client and the removed default client scope. Run the secret operations on a dedicated client, or restore the secret and register a cleanup.
